scope:
Design review (S3R) of specs/011-declared-documents plan.md, research.md, tasks.md and decisions.md against spec.md, across all three lenses (spec-compliance, security, architecture). Each finding's lens is its id prefix: SPEC, SEC, ARCH. Read: mvp_compliance/models.py, admin.py, apps.py, exceptions.py, checks.py, migrations/0001 and 0002; demo/settings.py, demo/templates/demo/landing.html, demo/management/commands/seed_demo.py; tests/settings.py, factories.py, conftest.py (names only); ADR 0003, 0019. Resolved Django is 6.1.2 (.venv django/__init__.py:3). I read these Django files: core/management/commands/migrate.py:98-389, core/management/sql.py, core/management/commands/flush.py:55-91, db/backends/base/creation.py:78-100, db/migrations/executor.py:75-80, test/testcases.py:1265-1286, db/models/fields/__init__.py:812-878 and 1247-1251 and 2487-2496, db/models/query.py:833-935, 991-1047 and 1095-1139, contrib/admin/options.py:443-459, contrib/sites/management.py, contrib/auth/apps.py, contrib/contenttypes/apps.py. Coverage: FR against tasks 16 of 16 (each has a task. FR-011's declared-and-published case has no test of its own, but the existing published guard refuses it anyway). SC against tasks 5 of 5. US-1 acceptance scenarios against tests 10 of 11 (scenario 3 missing: SPEC-002). US-2 scenarios 4 of 4. Edge cases 5: recreated after delete (follows from the mechanism, no test), slug declared twice (a dict key, so it cannot happen), changed slug (T001 scenario 7 plus T003), own name not a conflict (T003), other database (no test: ARCH-002). New code checked against the tree: 8 of 8 lines in research.md's 'What already exists'. All 8 hold, and nothing the tree or Django already provides is being rebuilt. Not on the list: the seed_demo kind change (a note). Routes that change a slug, both sides checked: Model.save (guarded), save(update_fields) (guarded by the existing writes_slug test, models.py:246-248), QuerySet.update (guarded), bulk_update (calls update(), query.py:1046), update_or_create (calls save(update_fields=...), query.py:1136), admin change form (read-only plus save()), admin list_editable (DocumentAdmin has none), admin actions (only delete_selected), bulk_create(update_conflicts=True) (NOT guarded: SEC-001), _base_manager and a historical model in a data migration (not guarded, as ADR 0004 already accepts for versions). Routes added: none. The admin only gains a read-only field, under the existing change_document permission. Trust boundaries: the setting, which the developer controls. No request input, no new route, no new dependency, and the setting is safe when unset (an empty dict).

ANSWERS TO THE ORCHESTRATOR'S QUESTION, read from the resolved Django 6.1.2:
(1) Correct, with two qualifications. emit_post_migrate_signal (sql.py:42-59) sends once per app config with sender=app_config, so a receiver connected with sender=self runs once per migrate, per database: migrate.py:382-389 passes using=connection.alias and apps=post_migrate_apps. Test database creation calls migrate with run_syncdb=True (creation.py:91-97). With TEST MIGRATE=False every app is made unmigrated (creation.py:82-87) and becomes a real app in ProjectState (executor.py:80), and migrate.py:370-378 re-renders the real models, so apps.get_model still finds Document and FR-010 holds in that configuration too. flush emits post_migrate WITHOUT an apps argument (flush.py:89), so the receiver's default apps=global_apps is load-bearing: keep it. It emits only when sql_list is non-empty and inhibit_post_migrate is false (flush.py:85). TransactionTestCase inhibits it when available_apps is set, or under serialized_rollback with serialized contents (testcases.py:1270-1277). So 'after each flush' holds only for a TransactionTestCase with available_apps=None and no serialized rollback. Migrating mvp_compliance to zero: the post-migrate state holds no mvp_compliance models, the re-render (migrate.py:370-378) only re-registers real apps, and the receiver is still sent (sql.py:44 iterates the global app configs), so StateApps.get_model raises LookupError and the planned return is correct.
(2) The database is left fully migrated, not partly migrated, and no document is written. executor.migrate (migrate.py:355-361) has applied and recorded every migration, each in its own atomic block, before post_migrate is sent at 382. The plan checks every declaration before its transaction.atomic, so nothing is written. Two side effects: (a) post_migrate.send is not send_robust, so the exception also stops the emissions for every app listed after mvp_compliance in INSTALLED_APPS. contenttypes' create_contenttypes and auth's create_permissions are connected with no sender (contenttypes/apps.py:20, auth/apps.py:23-26) and run on every app's emission, so those later apps get no content types or permissions on the failing run until migrate runs again. (b) ImproperlyConfigured is not a CommandError, so migrate exits with a traceback that ends in the message. Rerunning migrate after the settings are fixed repairs both.
(3) Yes. Field.clean (fields/__init__.py:869-878) runs to_python, then validate(value, model_instance), then run_validators. The base validate (838-867) never reads model_instance: it checks choices, null and blank. run_validators uses self.validators = default_validators + the field's own (815-820). For slug that is validate_slug (2488), lowercase_slug, unreserved_slug and the MaxLengthValidator CharField appends (1251). For name it is MaxLengthValidator. No model instance is needed. Uniqueness is not checked, since that lives in Model.validate_unique, and the plan's own name check covers it. The caveat is in ARCH-003: Field.clean does not strip whitespace, which the admin's form field does.
(4) bulk_update goes through update() (query.py:1043-1046). update_or_create goes through save(update_fields=...) (query.py:1120-1136), which the existing writes_slug test covers. save(update_fields=[...without slug]) never writes the slug. DocumentAdmin has no list_editable and slug is not in list_display, so the changelist cannot edit it. One route is unguarded: bulk_create(update_conflicts=True, unique_fields=['name'], update_fields=['slug']) is an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE through _batched_insert (query.py:897-923) that calls neither save() nor update(). See SEC-001. _base_manager and a migration's historical model also bypass both guards, as they already do for the published lock.
(5) Yes, provided the declared names are exactly the ones seed_demo uses. plan.md's names ('Privacy policy', 'Terms of use', 'Impressum') match seed_demo.py:329-349, and the slugs match SLUGS at seed_demo.py:176-186. On an empty demo database, migrate creates the three with no version and kind AGREED. make_document's get_or_create(name=...) (seed_demo.py:516-518) then finds each one, sees no versions and seeds them. Without the planned kind change the Impressum would be published as a document people agree to, and the agree page would ask everyone to accept it. With the change made before versions are published, it is a notice, which is what T005's 'Done when' checks. On a demo database seeded earlier, every slug already exists and migrate creates nothing.

findings.claim: [architecture] The planned admin change shows a declared document's slug twice once it has a published version. That is the normal state of a declared privacy policy or terms of use.
findings.evidence: plan.md 'The slug lock': 'DocumentAdmin.get_readonly_fields(): add `slug` when the document's slug is declared'. Today get_readonly_fields already appends 'slug' when a version is published (admin.py:39-44). A second, independent append gives ['slug', 'slug'] for a declared and published document. Django builds the default fieldset from [*form.base_fields, *self.get_readonly_fields(request, obj)] (contrib/admin/options.py:451, get_fieldsets at 459), so the read-only slug row is drawn twice. T006 tests only a declared document with no version, so the suite stays green.
findings.reproduction: Declare 'privacy-policy', publish a version, open its change form in the admin: two read-only 'slug' rows.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md 'The slug lock', admin bullet: 'get_readonly_fields() adds `slug` once, when a version is published or the slug is declared'. One condition, one append. In T006, also assert that get_readonly_fields() names 'slug' exactly once for a document that is both declared and published.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] US-2 depends on an interface US-1 introduces, and both stories edit the same files, so they cannot be built as independent stories.
findings.evidence: tasks.md T002 (US-1) adds `declared_documents()` to mvp_compliance/models.py. T007 (US-2) builds the lock in Document.save() and DocumentQuerySet.update() in the same module on top of that reader, and DocumentAdmin.get_readonly_fields() reads it too. Both stories also edit docs/models.md, CONTEXT.md and CHANGELOG.md (T005, T007). tasks.md states no dependency between the stories.
findings.suggested_fix: tasks.md, US-2 heading: 'Depends on US-1 (T002's declared_documents()); built after US-1 is merged into the feature branch.' Alternatively, move `declared_documents()` and its unset/empty test into a foundational task ahead of both stories. One of the two, not both.

findings.claim: [architecture] The plan wraps the creation in transaction.atomic(using=using) but never says the receiver reads and writes on `using`. The default router could therefore send its queries to another database, and the spec's other-database edge case has no test.
findings.evidence: plan.md 'Creating declared documents' steps 2-5 and research.md 'How a declared document is created' name `using` only for the router check and the atomic block. The precedent the plan cites reads and writes through Site.objects.using(using) and .save(using=using) (contrib/sites/management.py:27, 35-37). Without that, a project with two databases and no router that runs `migrate --database=other` reads and writes 'default' (db_for_read and db_for_write fall back to DEFAULT_DB_ALIAS) while the atomic block guards 'other'. spec.md Edge Cases: 'gets the declared documents wherever the package's documents are kept'.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md steps 2, 3 and 5: 'every query and the create go through `Document.objects.using(using)`, as create_default_site does'. Text only. No new test is asked for, because the test settings hold one database.

findings.claim: [security] SC-004 says no route moves a declared slug, but QuerySet.bulk_create(update_conflicts=True, update_fields=['slug']) moves one, past both planned guards. The same hole already exists in the published-slug lock.
findings.evidence: query.py:883-923: bulk_create with update_conflicts writes through _batched_insert as an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, calling neither Model.save() nor QuerySet.update(). Document.objects.bulk_create([Document(name='Privacy policy', slug='elsewhere')], update_conflicts=True, unique_fields=['name'], update_fields=['slug']) rewrites the declared row's slug. plan.md's lock covers save(), update(), bulk_update() and the admin. ADR 0019 names the same three code routes. This needs consumer code that deliberately upserts on name, so it is low.
findings.suggested_fix: No new guard. In T007's docs/models.md 'When the slug is fixed', name the routes that refuse (save(), update(), bulk_update(), the admin) and state that bulk_create(update_conflicts=True) and a data migration's historical model are not guarded, as ADR 0004 already says for versions. Reword SC-004's evidence in decisions.md to 'every route the package's model and admin offer'.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] No planned test covers US-1 acceptance scenario 3, where publishing a version of a declared document makes its address show that version.
findings.evidence: tasks.md T001 lists scenarios 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 11. T003 covers 9 and 10. Scenario 3 appears in no task. The behaviour is the existing page for any published document, so a regression is unlikely, but nothing ties it to a declared document.
findings.suggested_fix: T001: add one case. Publish a version of a document the receiver created and assert that its address returns 200 with that version in the context. Or record in tasks.md which existing tests/test_views.py test covers it.

findings.claim: [architecture] Checking a declared name with the model field's clean() is not 'the blank check the admin already runs'. It accepts a whitespace-only name, and a name with stray spaces that the admin would have stripped.
findings.evidence: research.md 'Checking a declaration before anything is written' says Field.clean runs 'the blank check the admin already runs'. Field.validate refuses only values in empty_values (fields/__init__.py:866-867), and CharField.to_python does not strip. The admin's form field strips first (forms.CharField strip=True). So a declaration {'privacy-policy': '   '} creates a document named '   ', and 'Privacy policy ' creates a near-duplicate of an existing 'Privacy policy' without being reported as a conflict. The slug is unaffected, because validate_slug refuses whitespace.
findings.suggested_fix: plan.md step 3: 'the name is stripped before it is checked and created'. In T003, the empty-name case also covers a whitespace-only name.

notes: plan.md 'The demo' says seed_demo 'sets a found document's kind when it differs'. research.md says the kind of a document 'it is about to seed'. The research wording is the safe one: the change has to come after make_document's early return for a document that already has versions (seed_demo.py:519-521), or a re-seed sets Delivery information back to agreed until the final update at line 398.

ADR 0019's Decision paragraph ('can be changed freely until a version of the document is published') stops being the whole rule. A declared slug is fixed from the start. Either amend it to read as the current rule or add an ADR for the declared case. Nothing in the tasks touches it.
ADR 0003 lists two exceptions, and exceptions.py holds four and will hold five. This was already stale before this feature.

research.md says the receiver runs 'once per migrate'. It runs once per migrate per database, and after a flush only when the TransactionTestCase has available_apps=None and no serialized rollback (testcases.py:1270-1277).

FR-015 docs: say that when a declaration is refused, the migrations have already been applied, and that running migrate again after fixing the settings completes what was skipped (including content types and permissions for apps listed after mvp_compliance).
migrate is decorated @no_translations, so the ImproperlyConfigured message always shows in English. FR-014 is still met by marking the strings.

plan.md says the declared check comes before the published one, so a declared and published document refuses a slug change with DeclaredDocumentError. No test pins which exception wins. FR-011 holds either way.

The test that the receiver is connected (T001's call_command('migrate')) proves the wiring in apps.py, so the testing standard's mirroring rule points at tests/test_app.py rather than tests/test_management.py.
research.md 'What already exists' has no line for the seed_demo kind change.
